question: The position vectors of the points $P$ and $Q$ are $2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$ and $-4\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, respectively.(a) Find the position vector of the point $R$ that divides $PQ$ internally in the ratio $2:1$.(b) Find the position vector of the point $S$ that divides $PQ$ externally in the ratio $2:1$.(c) Determine the position vector of the midpoint of $PQ$.
explanation: (a)Let $\vec{p}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$ and $\vec{q}=-4\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+\hat{k}$. If $R$ divides $PQ$ internally in the ratio $2:1$, then`\vec{r}=\frac{2\vec{q}+\vec{p}}{2+11}\vec{r}=\frac{2(-4\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+\hat{k})+(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k})}{3}\vec{r}=\frac{-6\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+6\hat{k}}{3}\vec{r}=-2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+2\hat{k}`Final ResultThe position vector of $R$ is $-2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$.(b)If $S$ divides $PQ$ externally in the ratio $2:1$, then`\vec{s}=\frac{2\vec{q}-\vec{p}}{2-1}\vec{s}=2(-4\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+\hat{k})-(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k})\vec{s}=-10\hat{i}+11\hat{j}-2\hat{k}`Final ResultThe position vector of $S$ is $-10\hat{i}+11\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$.(c)The midpoint divides $PQ$ internally in the ratio $1:1$. Therefore, its position vector is`\frac{\vec{p}+\vec{q}}{2}=\frac{(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k})+(-4\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+\hat{k})}{2}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\frac{5}{2}\hat{k}`Final ResultThe position vector of the midpoint is $-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\frac{5}{2}\hat{k}$.
